title: Titanique on Broadway #titanique #titaniquemusical #broadwayreview #t...
transcript: Just because you turn the volume up to 11, doesn't make it a Broadway show. This rollicking, already cult-classic musical splashes onto the Great White Way with showstopping vocals and a boatload of cultural references. It’s a parody of the film Titanic, featuring none other than Celine Dion, who proclaims she was on the ship and saw everything go down with Jack and Rose. It stars Marla Mindelle who has some serious pipes and comedic chops, though some of the humor is a little millennial, for lack of a better term. The entire cast is great, though I especially enjoyed Jim Parsons as Rose's mother, completely vicious and unhinged. I was pretty shocked to hear this was transferring since it already had an extensive run downtown. While I'm glad this gave me the chance to finally see it, I do wish I'd seen its earlier run. Of course, things like the lavish set and ooh- inducing lighting design are epic on a large scale, but the show at its core relies on its comedic sensibility to smooth over its somewhat haphazard storytelling. A cavernous Broadway theatre is not where this type of comedy and audience interaction thrives. In fairness, The St James is one of the largest Broadway theatres, dwarfing most theatrical productions. And when you throw in as much comedy and fierce vocals as this show has, you can almost get away with it — I had a good time. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer enjoyed the show despite some reservations about the Broadway transfer, praising the vocals, cast performances, and having 'a good time' overall. The criticism about venue size and comedy style are presented as caveats rather than deal-breakers.
